title: Stream Telemetry Load Synthesizer: realistic SSE/WS chat traffic with p95 regression gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible load harness that synthesizes realistic streaming chat traffic (SSE + WebSocket) to exercise the serving runtime and the routing layers. Goals: measure tokens/sec under steady-state and burst conditions, track tail latency (p95/p99) for response start and token stream deltas, detect regressions versus a baseline, and surface actionable traces and metrics for performance tuning. The harness should run on our k8s QA cluster, produce Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards, and integrate with regression-alerting (Slack + PagerDuty) when key signals deviate by configured thresholds.
metrics_targets: Steady-state throughput: 45k tokens/sec across 64 dedicated workers (baseline 2026-02-10)
Start-to-first-token p95 < 220ms under 99% of test windows
Inter-token p95 < 30ms for small-step streams (<=20 tokens), p95 < 120ms for long streams (>=512 tokens)
Connection churn handling: 30% simulated reconnects with <1% request failures
KV cache hit ratio >= 65% for prefix-heavy workload
False-positive regression rate for alerts < 5% per month
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a reproducible 1-hour soak on k8s-qa with both SSE and WebSocket modes and produce a recorded baseline snapshot (tokens/sec, p95, error-rate)
Generated metrics are exported to Prometheus with labels: protocol, model_variant, client_profile, seq_len_bucket, region
Grafana dashboard shows time-aligned comparison between current run and baseline and supports ad-hoc windowed regression queries
Automated regression detection job runs post-run and creates a GitHub issue with diffed metric graphs and raw traces when thresholds exceeded
Test harness includes a configurable chaos module (latency jitter, connection drop, TLS session reuse toggles) and can be toggled in YAML
End-to-end test of alerting pipeline: regression -> Slack channel -> PagerDuty incident (staged)
Documentation (README + runbook) published in Confluence and linked in the ticket
tasks: Design traffic profiles: small-chat (8-32 tokens), medium (64-128), long-form (256-1024); create per-profile token distribution and prefix reuse rates
Implement client emulator with pluggable protocol adapters (SSE, WS) and multiplexing layer for connection reuse
Add sequence-length aware pacing and token emission modeling to client emulator
Integrate Prometheus client: emit histograms for start-latency, inter-token delta, tokens/sec, connection_succeeds/fails
Create baseline job runner and store baseline snapshots in GCS (path: gs://redwood-load/baselines/streaming/2026-02-10)
Implement regression detector: compare recent run windows to baseline using percent-change and Mann-Whitney U for latency distributions
Build Grafana comparisons dashboard and a small web UI that can overlay runs
Add chaos knobs: client-side jitter, server drop simulation (calls to test hook), TLS session reuse toggle
Wire up CI job and nightly cron (k8s CronJob) to run smoke and extended runs; ensure artifacts uploaded to artifact store
Write runbook and playbook: how to interpret alert diffs, rollbacks, and temporary mitigations (route to fallback model variant, reduce batch size)
End-to-end test: run harness in staging, create synthetic regression, verify GitHub issue + Slack + PagerDuty flow
risks: Cluster resource limits: harness might saturate k8s-qa node egress or GPU pools and produce non-deterministic results
False positives from noisy baselines if workload distribution changes quickly
Instrumenting production-like telemetry labels might add cardinality explosion in Prometheus
Emulator timing precision on small VMs may not reflect real client TCP behaviors
Chaos module could accidentally be enabled in a production linked environment without safeguards
implementation_notes: Prefer Go for the emulator for low-latency timers; use existing async WS client library used in ENG-51784 where possible
Reuse existing Prometheus-k8s exporters pattern from runtime team to keep metric naming consistent
Store raw per-request traces (sampling 5%) in Tempo-compatible format so Grafana can display spans
Baseline comparison will use percent-change thresholds by metric and a non-parametric test for latency distributions to robustly detect shifts
Avoid heavy cardinality by bucketing client profiles and sequence lengths into coarse enums (short/medium/long)
Security: harness will use a dedicated test API key scoped to QA only; mark security_review_required = true and add gating for any push to prod-like clusters

notes: Keep runs reproducible: seed synthetic user IDs and prompt prefixes and record RNG seeds in artifacts
Avoid storing raw user content — use templated synthetic prompts derived from public prompt corpora
Coordinate with runtime release window to avoid testing during production deployments
